sprint_note: Adds a read-only Today/Upcoming agenda endpoint (GET /api/tasks/agenda) and recurring tasks (4 new columns, recurrence fields on POST/PATCH, atomic successor spawn on completion), plus the matching Today tab, Repeat control and next-date toast.
summary: Lightweight single-user task management application that creates, tracks, labels, schedules and recurs tasks, shows a Today/Upcoming agenda, persists tasks in Postgres and delegates label management to LabelEngine, user preferences to PreferenceStore, and calendar blocking to CalendarConnector.

classification.why_application: Owns task domain state (tasktracker.tasks) and task-specific rules: agenda bucketing by effective date, recurrence date arithmetic, successor spawning, and recurrence validation. Contains no reusable infrastructure.
non_goals: Server-side label filtering on GET /tasks or GET /tasks/agenda — label filtering stays client-side
Reverse calendar sync — changes in Google Calendar do not flow back to Atlas
LinkingEngine integration — task.id is used directly as atlas_event_id
Retry logic for failed calendar or label calls
Background job scheduler — auto-promotion stays lazy on fetch
[NEW] Weekday sets, end dates/counts, nth-weekday rules (future work)
[NEW] Skipping one occurrence, editing 'this and future'
[NEW] HabitTracker integration — streak-style habits stay in HabitTracker; no cross-app calls
[NEW] Today view entries for undated in_progress tasks
[NEW] Calendar cleanup on task DELETE (still deferred from Sprint10)
classification.not_platform: Agenda bucketing, recurrence arithmetic and successor spawning encode TaskTracker domain meaning (effective date, task statuses, task_type) and are not reusable platform capability. Label copy and calendar blocker creation reuse existing platform services via their existing HTTP APIs.

[CHANGED] POST /api/tasks — also accepts recurrence_freq, recurrence_interval, recurrence_mode

[CHANGED] PATCH /api/tasks/{task_id} — also accepts the three recurrence fields; completing a recurring task spawns exactly one successor atomically; response row carries recurrence_next_date when a successor was spawned by this request

invariants: All GET endpoints return Dataset | ApiError per R-CON-BP-04
task.id is a UUID generated at insert time; never caller-supplied
task.status in {open, in_progress, scheduled, pending, done}; task.priority in {low, medium, high}; effort_hours >= 0; title non-blank
On POST, status is restricted to open, pending, or scheduled (done is never a creation state, so POST never spawns)
PATCH distinguishes field omitted (no change) from explicit null (clear) via model_fields_set
task.updated_at is set server-side to now() on every PATCH
Calendar sync is best-effort and runs only after a successful DB commit
[NEW] Effective date (agenda) = scheduled_at when status = 'scheduled', otherwise due_date. This is the single definition used by GET /api/tasks/agenda.
[NEW] Agenda time authority is the server: 'today' = Postgres current_date, evaluated once inside the agenda query transaction. The client never computes buckets.

[NEW] Agenda contains only tasks with status != 'done', task_type != 'training_unit', non-null effective date, and effective date <= today + 7 days. Bucket: effective < today = overdue; = today = today; > today = upcoming.

[NEW] A task is recurring iff recurrence_freq is not null. Recurring tasks have task_type = 'normal' (API-enforced). recurrence_mode = 'fixed' requires due_date or scheduled_at at write time unless the resulting status is 'done'.
[NEW] When recurrence_freq resolves to null, recurrence_interval is stored as 1 and recurrence_mode as 'fixed' regardless of values sent.

[NEW] A successor is spawned only on the PATCH that transitions status from non-done to done, when the post-update row has recurrence_freq not null and recurrence_next_id null. The source row is read with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, so concurrent completions cannot spawn two successors.
[NEW] Successor INSERT, source recurrence_next_id UPDATE and the status UPDATE commit in one transaction; either all persist or none.

[NEW] The successor is an independent row: status 'open' (or 'scheduled' when the source had a schedule date), completed_at null, actual_duration_minutes null, recurrence_next_id null, task_type 'normal', same title/description/priority/effort_hours/parent_task_id/recurrence_* as the post-update source row.
[NEW] Next-date rule is defined once by compute_next_date in backend/recurrence.py (see 10_scaffolding.json); the 'today' input comes from the DB (select current_date) in the spawn transaction.

[NEW] Undo (done -> other) and re-done never spawn a second successor while recurrence_next_id is non-null. Deleting the successor nulls the pointer (ON DELETE SET NULL), after which a re-done of the source spawns a new successor.
[NEW] Clearing recurrence (recurrence_freq: null) does not touch recurrence_next_id.
[NEW] recurrence_label is derived server-side by format_recurrence_label on every task row; null when not recurring.

VALIDATION_ERROR — POST or PATCH with invalid field values, status=scheduled without scheduled_at, no fields provided — 400 ApiError

NOT_FOUND — PATCH or DELETE on unknown task_id — 404 ApiError

[NEW] LabelEngine unreachable during successor label copy — warning logged, successor exists without labels, PATCH succeeds
[NEW] CalendarConnector failure on successor blocker create — warning logged, PATCH succeeds

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/tasks
exposed_surfaces.purpose: List tasks with optional status or view filter and pagination; labels embedded. Behaviour unchanged except rows now include recurrence fields.

row_shape.title: str
row_shape.recurrence_next_date: [NEW] str|null (ISO date; non-null ONLY in the single-row PATCH response that spawned a successor, i.e. successor scheduled_at when scheduled else due_date; null in every other response)

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/tasks/agenda
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Return the agenda window (overdue, today, next 7 days) as one flat Dataset ordered for direct sectioned rendering. Runs auto-promotion first (and commits it), then one SELECT. Parameters: none (any query string is ignored). Pagination: none (window is bounded). Ordering: agenda_date ASC, then priority high>medium>low, then created_at ASC, then id ASC. Grouping: server returns a flat list; client sections by agenda_bucket and groups upcoming rows by agenda_date; days without tasks are not emitted (no zero-fill). Empty result: 200 with rows [] and meta.total 0. Totals: client sums effort_hours (null = 0) over displayed rows per bucket and per upcoming day.

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/tasks
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Create a task. Body additionally accepts recurrence_freq (str|null, default null), recurrence_interval (int, default 1), recurrence_mode (str, default 'fixed'). Recurrence validation per contracts.failure_modes. Returns created task as single-row Dataset.

exposed_surfaces.name: PATCH /api/tasks/{task_id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Partial update. Null-vs-omit for recurrence fields: recurrence_freq omitted = unchanged, value = set, explicit null = clear recurrence (interval/mode normalised to 1/'fixed', recurrence_next_id untouched). recurrence_interval and recurrence_mode omitted = unchanged, value = set, explicit null = VALIDATION_ERROR (columns are NOT NULL). due_date explicit null now clears due_date (previously ignored). Frontend always sends all three recurrence fields from the edit form; 'None' sends recurrence_freq: null, recurrence_interval: 1, recurrence_mode: 'fixed'. When this request transitions the task to done and a successor is spawned, the response row's recurrence_next_date is set. Returns single-row Dataset.

exposed_surfaces.name: DELETE /api/tasks/{task_id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Delete a task. Returns empty Dataset on success.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/tasks/labels/search
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Search labels by name prefix via LabelEngine.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/tasks/labels/used
exposed_surfaces.purpose: All labels attached to at least one task; empty Dataset on LabelEngine failure.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/tasks/{task_id}/labels
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Labels attached to one task via LabelEngine.

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/tasks/{task_id}/labels
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Attach a label by name via LabelEngine.

exposed_surfaces.name: PUT /api/tasks/{task_id}/labels
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Replace all labels on a task via LabelEngine.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/tasks/preferences/label_filter
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Retrieve stored label filter from PreferenceStore.

internal_flow.name: startup_init
internal_flow.description: On FastAPI startup: init_pool() then init_schema() executes schema.sql idempotently (now includes the four recurrence columns). Errors logged; application continues.

internal_flow.name: task_list
internal_flow.description: [CHANGED] GET /tasks unchanged except the shared TASK_SELECT_COLS now include the four recurrence columns and row_to_dict adds recurrence_label / recurrence_next_date (null).
outputs: Dataset with task rows and embedded labels

internal_flow.name: task_create
internal_flow.description: [CHANGED] POST /tasks validates existing fields plus recurrence (step 10), inserts the row including recurrence_* (interval/mode normalised to 1/'fixed' when freq is null), commits, then calendar create when status=scheduled. Returns single-row Dataset.

internal_flow.name: task_update
internal_flow.description: [CHANGED] PATCH /tasks/{task_id}: (a) body-only validation incl. recurrence enums/interval (step 10); (b) build field set via model_fields_set (due_date and the three recurrence fields use model_fields_set; null semantics per exposed_surfaces PATCH); (c) open transaction, read snapshot with SELECT * ... FOR UPDATE (404 if absent); (d) merged-state recurrence validation (step 10); (e) compute completed_at as before; (f) UPDATE ... RETURNING * ; (g) if spawn condition holds run step 11 inside the same transaction; (h) single commit; (i) post-commit side effects: existing calendar create/update/delete decisions from the pre-update snapshot, then step 12 for the successor. Returns single-row Dataset (with recurrence_next_date when spawned) or 404.

internal_flow.name: task_delete
internal_flow.description: Unchanged. DELETE removes the row; FK ON DELETE SET NULL clears any recurrence_next_id pointing at it. No calendar cleanup (deferred).

internal_flow.name: calendar_sync
internal_flow.description: Unchanged helper _sync_calendar_event(task_id, title, scheduled_at, description, action). Now also invoked for the successor with action 'create'.

internal_flow.name: label_proxy
internal_flow.description: Unchanged thin proxies to LabelEngine with object_type=task.

internal_flow.name: agenda_query
internal_flow.description: [NEW] GET /tasks/agenda: (1) get_db connection; (2) _run_auto_promotion(conn) then conn.commit() so promotion persists (existing list views do not commit, see risks); (3) one SELECT of TASK_SELECT_COLS plus effective date as agenda_date, filtered by status != 'done', task_type != 'training_unit', effective date not null, effective date <= current_date + 7; agenda_bucket derived from comparing effective date with current_date in the same statement; ordered per exposed_surfaces; (4) fetch_labels_for_tasks batch (failure -> empty labels); (5) build Dataset with AGENDA_SCHEMA, object_type 'task', label 'Agenda', total = row count, page 1, page_size max(total, 1), row_actions ['edit','delete'].
outputs: Dataset (flat rows with agenda_bucket, agenda_date) | ApiError

internal_flow.name: recurrence_validation
internal_flow.description: [NEW] Body-level: freq in VALID_RECURRENCE_FREQ when not null; mode in VALID_RECURRENCE_MODE; interval >= 1; explicit null interval/mode rejected. Merged-state (PATCH: snapshot overlaid with body; POST: body): if resulting freq not null then task_type must be 'normal'; and if mode is 'fixed' and resulting status != 'done' then due_date or scheduled_at must be non-null. Resulting freq null -> interval/mode forced to 1/'fixed'. All failures return VALIDATION_ERROR via api_error.

internal_flow.name: recurrence_spawn
internal_flow.description: [NEW] Inside the PATCH transaction after the status UPDATE, when pre.status != 'done' and post.status == 'done' and post.recurrence_freq is not null and post.recurrence_next_id is null: (1) today = select current_date; (2) schedule_date = post.scheduled_at, else pre.scheduled_at if pre.status == 'scheduled', else none (the edit form clears scheduled_at on save, hence the snapshot fallback); (3) anchor = schedule_date if present else post.due_date (may be none); (4) next = compute_next_date(anchor, freq, interval, mode, today); (5) if schedule_date present: successor status 'scheduled', scheduled_at = next, due_date = post.due_date + (next - schedule_date) in days when post.due_date present else null; otherwise successor status 'open', scheduled_at null, due_date = next; (6) INSERT successor (new uuid) with fields per invariants; (7) UPDATE source SET recurrence_next_id = successor.id (no updated_at bump beyond the one already applied). No spawn if any condition fails (including done->done PATCH, non-recurring, freq cleared in the same request, pointer already set).

internal_flow.name: successor_side_effects
internal_flow.description: [NEW] After commit, only when a successor was spawned: (a) if successor is scheduled, _sync_calendar_event(successor_id, title, next, description, 'create') (best-effort); (b) _copy_labels_best_effort(source_id, successor_id): GET source labels from LabelEngine, POST each label name to the successor with object_type=task; any exception logged and swallowed. Order relative to the source's own calendar delete is irrelevant (different event ids).

internal_required.role: Shared Postgres; TaskTracker owns the tasktracker schema
All label data incl. copying labels onto recurrence successors

internal_optional.role: Calendar blocker for scheduled tasks and scheduled recurrence successors; best-effort

external_required.name: httpx
external_required.role: HTTP client for LabelEngine, PreferenceStore, CalendarConnector

forbidden: Frontend calling LabelEngine, PreferenceStore, or CalendarConnector directly

Client-side computation of agenda buckets or of 'today' for the agenda
Spawning successors from a background job or on read — spawn happens only inside the completing PATCH transaction
Re-implementing label storage or preference storage in TaskTracker

risks.risk: Literal effective-date definition hides scheduled tasks due today: auto-promotion turns status 'scheduled' (scheduled_at <= today) into 'in_progress', whose effective date is due_date, so a scheduled-for-today task without due_date does not appear in Today, and the Overdue/Today buckets can never contain status 'scheduled' rows
risks.impact: A task the user scheduled for today may be invisible in the Today view. Implemented literally per draft; fix is a one-expression change (effective date = coalesce(scheduled_at, due_date) for non-done tasks) because the expression is defined once in internal_flow step 9. See open_questions.

risks.risk: Existing list_tasks views call _run_auto_promotion but never commit; get_db returns the connection to the pool, which rolls back an open transaction, so promotion appears applied in the response but is not persisted
risks.impact: Unverified on a live DB by the designer. The agenda endpoint commits explicitly so its promotion persists, which makes agenda and other views disagree about stored status until the other views are touched. Existing views are intentionally unchanged this sprint (draft: existing views/tests unaffected).

risks.risk: Edit form clears scheduled_at on save when status != 'scheduled'; completing a scheduled recurring task via the edit form would lose the schedule date
risks.impact: Mitigated by the snapshot fallback in recurrence_spawn step (pre.scheduled_at used when pre.status == 'scheduled'); a promoted in_progress task whose scheduled_at was already cleared falls back to due_date anchor or, with no date, to today + interval.

risks.risk: Month arithmetic computed from the original anchor (not cumulatively) intentionally differs from a naive 'keep adding' loop
risks.impact: Results differ only after clamping (Jan 31 -> Feb 28 -> Mar 31 instead of Mar 28); this is the same 'first date > today' outcome the draft asks for, without day-of-month drift.

risks.risk: Deleting a successor nulls the source pointer, so a later undo+redo of the source spawns a fresh successor
risks.impact: Acceptable for a single-user app; idempotency guard only protects against duplicate live successors.

risks.risk: Label copy and calendar create happen after commit and are best-effort
risks.impact: A successor can exist without labels or without a calendar blocker if those services are down; no retry this sprint.

risks.risk: Moving Active from /tasks to /tasks/active changes the default landing path
risks.impact: Any bookmark or external link to /tasks now lands on Today. No other repository consumer of the Active path was found (searched 02_Platform and 03_Application for '/tasks' route usage).

open_questions.question: Should the effective date for promoted tasks (status in_progress with scheduled_at retained by promotion) fall back to scheduled_at so that tasks scheduled for today stay visible in Today? Design implements the draft literally (scheduled_at only while status='scheduled').
Should dated tasks with status 'pending' appear in the agenda? Draft excludes only done and training_unit, so the design includes them (and includes task_type 'training_session').

Confirm that persisting auto-promotion from the agenda endpoint (explicit commit) is acceptable while the existing active/pending_board views keep their current non-committing behaviour, or should those be fixed in a follow-up sprint?

The draft says PATCH explicit null clears nullable fields but the current implementation ignores due_date: null. The design fixes due_date null-clearing (needed so removing a date removes a task from the agenda and from fixed-mode recurrence). Confirm no caller depends on due_date: null being ignored (grep of 03_Application/PersonalDevelopment/frontend found no due_date usage).
